bugs: app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:59 – the message reads $this->event->payload['payment_id'] directly. If an event has no payment_id, this throws ErrorException 'Undefined array key' (confirmed by a probe). On a real worker that error is retried with backoff up to MaxExceptions(5) instead of failing permanently, and the stored error text tells you nothing useful.

app/Enums/WebhookEventStatus.php:12 / ProcessWebhookEvent.php:47 – isFinished() includes Failed, so running queue:retry on a permanently failed job does nothing and the event stays failed for good (confirmed by a probe). recover-stuck also skips failed events, so there is no way to reprocess them.
app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:33 – the receipt currency is hard-coded to EUR.

Every 10 minutes, webhooks:recover-stuck re-dispatches Received events that are simply waiting behind the rate limiter in a long backlog. That puts duplicate jobs on the queue. They are harmless because of WithoutOverlapping and the isFinished check, but they add load.
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/RecoverStuckWebhookEvents.php:1 – a custom recovery command plus a 10-minute schedule that does work queue retry_after and failed_jobs already do. This is over-engineering.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:51-52 – sets status and then calls touch() to persist it. That relies on a side effect of touch(); an explicit save or update would be clearer.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:57-60 – one nested ternary builds two unrelated failure messages.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:65 – the provider HTTP call is inline in the job, so it is harder to reuse or fake per service.
app/Models/Order.php:67 – a hand-rolled transitionFrom state machine using raw conditional updates. It is robust but adds ceremony beyond what the task asks for.
routes/console.php:12-16 – dailyAt plus a hard-coded timezone, onOneServer and withoutOverlapping on a simple prune is ceremony.
strengths: Uses modern queue attributes (#[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions], #[Timeout], #[DeleteWhenMissingModels]) together with retryUntil, so releases from the middleware don't use up a tries budget.
WithoutOverlapping plus RateLimited middleware; a 429 releases the job using Retry-After.
The conditional-update order transitions guarantee only one receipt per order; the notification is ShouldQueueAfterCommit.
Uses createOrFirst on a unique event_id with a wasRecentlyCreated guard; MassPrunable plus a scheduled model:prune.

The best tests: they run a real database queue worker, assert exact backoff delays (10, then 30), the 429 Retry-After release, the rate limit across 11 jobs, the overlap lock via getLockKey, and duplicate job dispatch.
A thorough README that covers nested timeouts and warns against passing --tries to the worker.

bugs: app/Http/Requests/StoreWebhookEventRequest.php:14 – 'data' => required|array rejects an empty data object {} with a 422. The provider would keep redelivering it. This is minor and shared by all three implementations.
README.md – the Supervisor example passes --tries=3 to the worker. The job's retryUntil overrides it, so it does no harm, but it is misleading next to the job-level retry policy.
antipatterns: bootstrap/app.php:14 – registers a separate routes/webhooks.php through then: and Route::group([]). This adds ceremony compared with putting the route in web.php and excluding it from CSRF; it works because the file is loaded without the web group.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:56 – status is set to Processing outside the transaction and stays Processing while transient retries are pending (acceptable, but not cleaned up).
strengths: Clean PaymentProvider service; transient (5xx/429/connection) and permanent (4xx) errors are split, and permanent ones go to PermanentWebhookException and then $this->fail().
Real idempotency: inside a transaction it re-reads the event with lockForUpdate and locks the order row, on top of WithoutOverlapping. Refunds are deduplicated by provider_refund_id.

Uses retryUntil, not tries, because releases from RateLimited/WithoutOverlapping count as attempts; this is documented in a single-line comment. Uses #[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions], #[Timeout] and #[DeleteWhenMissingModels].
Unlike impl-1 and impl-3, failed events can be reprocessed with queue:retry, because only Processed short-circuits.
ShouldQueueAfterCommit receipt; the #[Scope] withStatus scope is reused in prunable and the index; the form request exposes typed status()/perPage() accessors.

Excellent tests: a real database queue checks increasing delays, retry exhaustion leading to Failed, 12 jobs held to 10 per second, and a pre-held overlap lock skipping the job; prune and schedule are tested too.
The README covers Supervisor, the shared cache requirement, queue:restart, the scheduler, the timeout and retry_after relationship, and the retry semantics.

bugs: app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:56 / ProcessWebhookEvent.php:43 – isFinished() treats Failed as finished, so queue:retry on a failed job does nothing (confirmed by a probe). The README explicitly says to use queue:retry for such jobs, which contradicts the code.

app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:25 – #[Tries(30)] with no retryUntil. Every release from RateLimited or WithoutOverlapping uses an attempt, so a large backlog (hundreds of events at 10 per second) can exhaust 30 attempts. Those events then fail with MaxAttemptsExceeded even though the provider never errored.
The is-it-processed check and markProcessed don't use a row lock or transactional re-read. Idempotency depends entirely on the cache lock from WithoutOverlapping, which can expire (expireAfter 120).
antipatterns: app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:13 – implements both ShouldQueue and ShouldQueueAfterCommit; the second already extends the first.
app/Http/Controllers/PaymentWebhookController.php:16 – stores the whole validated envelope as payload, so id and type are duplicated and the job has to use data_get('data.payment_id').

tests/Feature/PaymentWebhookTest.php – some tests are reflection-based (they read attribute arguments) or mock the middleware with Mockery instead of running a real worker. They test configuration, not behaviour.
database/migrations/2026_11_07_000002_create_orders_table.php – creates the orders and refunds tables in one migration.
All tests are in one large file; the end-to-end test relies on the sync queue.
strengths: Simple, readable job; intent-revealing model methods (markProcessing, markProcessed, markFailed).
Guards against duplicate receipts by checking alreadyPaid; ShouldQueueAfterCommit inside the transaction.
Uses Rule::enum and per_page validation, the can: middleware, onOneServer on the prune, and MassPrunable.
Handles 4xx except 429 as permanent and 5xx as transient; the order lookup happens before the API call so no request is wasted.
A clear README covering Supervisor, the shared cache and the timeout chain.

v.rationale:
impl-2 ranks first. It is the only implementation that combines a transactional lockForUpdate re-check, retryUntil instead of a tries count (so middleware releases don't use up the retry budget), permanent failures through a domain exception, and failed events that can be reprocessed with queue:retry. Its tests run a real database queue worker to check backoff, retry exhaustion, the rate limit and the overlap lock. I found no real bugs beyond trivia that all three share.

impl-1 ranks second. It has the strongest test suite, uses retryUntil correctly, and handles 429 with Retry-After. It loses points for over-engineering (a stuck-event recovery command, a hand-rolled state machine, a timezone-pinned schedule). It also has two bugs confirmed by probes: a missing payment_id causes an ErrorException that gets retried instead of a clean permanent failure, and failed events can never be reprocessed.

impl-3 ranks third. Its code is simple and clean, but it has the same problem that failed events can't be reprocessed, and its README tells operators to use queue:retry, which then does nothing. Its #[Tries(30)] without retryUntil can wrongly fail events in a large backlog, because every rate-limit or overlap release uses an attempt. Its tests lean on reflection and Mockery more than running a real worker.

All three test suites pass (impl-2: 31 tests, impl-3: 37, impl-1: 37). I deleted all probe files afterwards.
